answer: A stake-and-history bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock collateral and build a verified record of completed work before it can earn trust or payments. A lone bot can wander in for free, but spawning a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand stakes and doing a thousand jobs — the cost grows like crossing a canyon with a full pack. Honest agents that keep delivering form a living reef of reputation, and newcomers must earn their place on it, so Sybil swarms drown in their own expense.
